request: the webhook fan-out and the artifact packaging path

defects.description: Relay.Broadcast posts each event to the endpoint a subscription stores after checking only that its text begins with https://, while the guarded delivery path (Relay.Deliver), the re-delivery route and every retry parse the URL with netguard and refuse a host that is not on the allowlist or that is a private, loopback, link-local or metadata address, so a subscription whose endpoint is https://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ is posted to by a broadcast although the README promises that every path that sends a delivery makes that decision on the parsed URL before anything is signed or sent.

trigger.input: cd bench/cases/x03-artifact-server && sh testdata/triggers/run.sh fixture  (variants: run.sh all | keep-D1 | keep-D2)
trigger.expected: D1 BroadcastEvent(https://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/) -> delivered=0 refused=1 posted=[] reason="notify: the endpoint is not allowed: netguard: endpoint is not allowed: \"169.254.169.254\" is a private or metadata address"

defects.why_missed: Every delivery test subscribes an endpoint whose host is the allowlisted one, so the prefix test and the guard agree on every value the suite sends; the guard itself has its own tests, which makes the policy look exercised while the fan-out path never consults it, and the metadata address only appears in the trigger harness.

defects.description: Packer.Repackage builds the packaging command by concatenating the artifact's name into a string handed to sh -c, while the tar, zip and bundle kinds hand the name to a tool as one argument of an argv list started without a shell, so an artifact named report.csv;printf pwned>injected.txt makes the shell run a second command and packs nothing, although the README promises that a tool runs with an argument list and that no stage builds a command string from a value a sender wrote.

trigger.input: cd bench/cases/x03-artifact-server && sh testdata/triggers/run.sh fixture  (variants: run.sh all | keep-D1 | keep-D2)
trigger.expected: D2 Repackage("report.csv;printf pwned>injected.txt") -> ok=true injected=false entries=[report.csv;printf pwned>injected.txt] reason=""
trigger.actual: D2 Repackage("report.csv;printf pwned>injected.txt") -> ok=true injected=true entries=[] reason=""

defects.why_missed: The packaging tests repack artifacts whose names the pipeline itself wrote (report.csv, bundle.tar), where a shell and an argv list produce the same archive, and the bundle kind's own test asserts the argv a runner received, which covers the sibling path and never the repackage command.
